title: Oncall shift handbook: node swap and warmstart (WIP)
content:
Purpose
This is a working oncall handbook for shift engineers to coordinate a safe node swap (hardware GPU replacement or node reprovision) while minimizing production impact via warmstart capacity and traffic handoffs. It focuses on fast triage, cordon/drain patterns that preserve KV/cache, graceful workload handoff, physical swap acceptance tests, and immediate post-incident actions.

Audience
Primary: oncall SREs and cross-zone responders. Secondary: infra techs (hardware team), release engineers, cluster-capacity owners.

Scope and assumptions
- Applies to heterogeneous clusters running inference workloads with KV cache (prefix caching) and sticky routing for certain tenant workloads.
- Assumes kubernetes-like control plane and a serving runtime that supports reconnecting sessions and KV cache warming.
- Assumes access to runbooks for network-level capacity (load-balancer), and hardware swap SOP (physical).

Signal/Triggers (examples)
- PagerDuty alert: sustained GPU ECC errors or NVLink failure on node -> P1 if throughput drop > 30% cluster-wide.
- Elevated 95th/99th latency for a model shard pinned to node X.
- Node marked NotReady with streaming reconnect errors for > 2 minutes.

Initial triage (first 10 minutes)
1) Acknowledge PD and post a minimal incident header in #sre-incident (who, what, what region, first-step owner).
2) Identify impacted node(s): kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep <node-name>. Check GPU health: nvidia-smi or node-exporter metrics.
3) Scope impact: which model routes are degraded? Query routing table and per-route latency dashboard.
4) If coverage gap predicted, immediately enable admission control for non-critical routes (rate-limit or pause batch jobs) to buy time.
5) Decide: soft-fallover (cordon + drain) or emergency-evacuate (force eviction) based on cache sensitivity and customer SLAs.

Preflight checklist (before cordon/drain)
- Notify hardware on-call and Eng-Platform if a physical swap may be needed.
- Confirm available warm nodes (spare capacity) in same AZ or cross-zone pool.
- Snapshot or mark KV cache hotkeys that belong to impacted workloads. Add note in incident channel: "KV-keyset snapshot started: <id>".
- Prepare rollback commands and a single-point-of-exit: how to uncordon quickly if needed.

Cordoning and draining (safe path)
Goal: move traffic away while preserving session continuity where possible.
1) kubectl cordon <node>  # prevents new pods
2) For stateful pods that support graceful handoff, run: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=15m
3) For inference worker pods that hold KV in local memory, use the runtime's cache-evac API to stream keys to warm nodes before eviction. Example: curl -X POST https://runtime.internal/cache/evacuate?node=<node>&targets=<pool-id>
4) Monitor re-scheduling and warm cache hit-rate on target nodes. If rescheduling fails or latency spikes, stop drain and revert.

Emergency evacuation (fast path)
- If the node is failing unpredictably (OOM, hardware hang), skip graceful cache transfer: kubectl drain <node> --force --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
- Immediately scale up warm nodes: k8s autoscaler trigger or infra-api call. Keep owners posted.

Physical GPU replacement handoff notes (coord with hardware team)
- Confirm exact part and firmware matching: GPU SKU, firmware version. If mismatch, request rollback image or hold replacement.
- Power cycle sequence: power off host -> cold swap -> power on -> BIOS confirmation. Hardware team to annotate ticket with serial/asset tags.
- Post-swap acceptance tests (hardware team + oncall): run GPU diagnostics (nvidia-smi -q), run small inference smoke test against model toy-suite (<5s p50). Record logs to artifact store.

Warmstart capacity and traffic shaping
- While replacement occurs, enable warmstart: pre-pull model shards to warm nodes with empty cache, then run 'cache-warm' jobs using representative prompts to pre-populate KV.
- Traffic shaping: route a percentage of traffic to warm nodes (canary 5/20/50) and measure latency/cost. If stable, increase gradually.
- If warm nodes in different AZ, enable autoscaling policies to keep coldstart under SLOs for cross-zone latency.

Verification checklist (acceptance)
- Node reports Ready and all GPU tests pass.
- Per-route 95th latency back within 5% of baseline.
- KV hit-rate restored to pre-incident level or within acceptable band.
- No increase in error-rate on canary customers.
- All scaled resources returned to normal (no orphaned pods, volumes detached).

Rollback plan
- If acceptance tests fail after uncordon: re-cordon node and shift traffic away. Use snapshot to restore cache to last-known-good nodes. Escalate to Hardware/RTE for deep debug.

Communication templates
Slack (incident channel) initial:
"PD Alert: GPU errors on node-az3-node-124. Owner: @aisha. Triage started. Impact: routes model-bert-v1 experiencing 95p latency increase. Action: cordon in progress, warming two spare nodes in az3. Linking SRE-4123"
PagerDuty escalation message:
"P1: Node hardware fault causing inference regressions in us-west-2. SRE oncall engaged. See #sre-incident for updates."
Post incident summary stub (to paste into ticket):
- What happened: single GPU ECC/thermal fault triggered node flapping and increased p95 latency for model-bert-v1.
- Root cause: suspected thermal event after firmware mismatch (investigation ongoing by hardware).
- Impact: 12% of cluster capacity in az3, 2% customer error elevation.
- Mitigation: cordon+drain, warmstart two nodes, physical GPU swap.
- Followups: firmware gating for new SKU, automated KV snapshot before cordon (SRE-4234).

Observability and metrics to collect (minimum)
- node_gpu_ecc_errors{node}, node_gpu_temperature{node}
- route_latency_p95{route}, route_error_rate
- cache_hit_rate{model_shard}
- pod_reschedule_time{node}
- cluster_available_capacity_percent{region}

Post-incident tasks and ownership
- (SRE) Add automatic KV snapshot hook to pre-drain pipeline (owner: @liam) — ticket SRE-4234.
- (Infra HW) Audit firmware for affected SKU and produce gating plan (owner: hardware-oncall).
- (Performance) Run regression evals on model-bert-v1 against warm nodes and produce cost delta report (owner: @marina).

Quick commands (cheat sheet)
- list pods on node: kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>
- cordon: kubectl cordon <node>
- drain: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120
- force drain: kubectl drain <node> --force --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
- check GPU health: ssh grunt@<node> sudo nvidia-smi -q
- scale warm pool: infractl capacity scale --pool warm-az3 --delta +2

Open questions / TODOs
- Can runtime support streaming cache replication (not full snapshot) to avoid coldstart penalty? (R&D exploration).
- Should we add automatic cross-AZ reheating when any GPU ECC errors are detected? Cost/benefit analysis required.
- Add a non-interactive mode for preflight checks to be run by automation.

Appendix: references and quick links
- Node replacement SOP (hardware): /confluence/hw/node-replace-sop
- Cache API docs: https://internal.docs/runtime/cache
- Incident ticket template: SRE-INCIDENT-TEMPLATE

Notes (freeform)
- This doc intentionally mixes high-level steps and quick commands to be useful in the heat of an active incident. Treat this as the single-pane oncall handbook for node swap runs.
- Keep this short and iterate; move longer lifecycle items into separate RFCs.

End of draft
